subject: economics
title: Circular Flow Foundations
welcome_lead: Money flows like a river between households and firms. Trace the loop and discover how the whole economy ticks.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics adventure on how the economy works: circular flow, AD components and the role of government.
final_note: You've mapped the flow. Time to do some macro maths!

concepts.def: Owners of factors of production, spend on goods.
Hire factors, produce goods and pay wages.
Where labour, land and capital are hired.
Where finished goods and services are sold.
Money entering the flow (I, G, X).
Money leaving the flow (S, T, M).

walkthroughs.body_html: Households sell their labour to firms in the factor market and receive wages. Firms make goods and sell them in the product market; households spend their wages there. Money circulates in a closed loop — total income = total spending = total output.

Real economies have injections (investment by firms, government spending, exports earnings) and withdrawals (household saving, taxes paid, imports bought). When injections = withdrawals, the economy is in equilibrium.

AD = C + I + G + (X − M). C is consumer spending (biggest chunk, ~60% UK). I is business investment. G is government spending. (X − M) is net exports. If imports exceed exports, that bracket is negative.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an INJECTION into the circular flow?
options: Saving
Imports
Government spending
Taxation

mcqs.q: In the formula AD = C + I + G + (X − M), what does C stand for?
options: Cost
Capital
Consumer spending
Currency

mcqs.q: What causes the supply curve to shift?
options: A recession is when the stock market crashes.
When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
Changes in production costs, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of producers, expectations — anything affecting supply other than the good's own price.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.

mcqs.q: What is the technical definition of a recession?
options: A recession is when the stock market crashes.
A recession is when prices fall and people lose jobs.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
Two consecutive quarters of negative real GDP growth — a contraction of the economy.

mcqs.q: What does dependency theory argue about development?
options: Poorer 'periphery' countries are kept underdeveloped by their economic relationships with rich 'core' countries — through unequal trade, debt and historical colonialism. It challenges the view that integration with rich economies automatically helps.
Dependency theory is about households relying on benefits.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
Dependency theory means poor countries are simply lazy.
